name: add_book_member
title: Add Book Member
description: Give an existing user access to a book. username must match exactly, including case. Owner only. Repeated failed attempts are rate-limited.

username.description: The exact username of an existing user. Case matters.

role.description: owner: everything, including members, rename, delete and bank connections. editor: read and change the ledger. viewer: read only.

name: analyze_usage
title: Analyze Usage
description: Query this server's PostHog project for usage events in the last `days` days. Returns totalEvents, eventCounts (each event name with its count, highest first) and recentEvents (the 20 newest events with their properties). eventType limits both to one event name, such as '$pageview' or 'transaction_created'. The data covers only the events of the calling user, across every book they use. The tool does not group by page or session; read page paths from the recentEvents properties.

days.description: Number of days to look back

name: clear_plaid_sync_data
title: Clear Plaid Sync Data
description: Discard every staged transaction for a connection and reset its sync cursor, so the next sync re-fetches from the beginning. Local transactions already reconciled are not affected. This touches only this database and never calls Plaid.

bookId.description: The book ID the connection belongs to

name: create_account
title: Create Account
description: Create an account in the chart of accounts. Creating an account with subtype 'investment' also creates its paired cash sub-account automatically. Use get_account_tree to find a parentId.

name.description: Account name, as it will appear in the chart of accounts.

type.description: Account type: asset, liability, equity, income, or expense. You cannot change this after creation.

subtype.description: Account subtype: bank, credit_card, loan, investment, cash, or other. Set to 'investment' to also create a paired cash sub-account automatically.

parentId.description: ID of the parent account, to nest this account under it. Omit for a top-level account. Use get_account_tree to find a parentId.

icon.description: A single emoji to show for this account. Only income and expense accounts show an icon. Send null to inherit the icon from the parent account instead of setting one directly.

name: create_book
title: Create Book
description: Create a new accounting book for the authenticated user. A book is the top-level container for a ledger — every account, transaction, security and bank connection belongs to one.

name.description: The book's name, shown in the book switcher and page titles.

name: create_demo_book
title: Create Demo Book
description: Create a new book and fill it with realistic sample data for exploring Counterpoise. The dates end today. `dataset` selects the sample: 'household' (the default) is a married couple with about three years of transactions across dozens of accounts, payees and securities; 'single' is one homeowner with a mortgage, a car lease and one credit card, with about two years of transactions. The book is named 'Demo Book' or 'Demo Book - Single', with ' 2', ' 3' and so on when that name is taken. This writes thousands of rows and can take several seconds.

name: create_issue_report
title: Create Issue Report
description: File a bug or improvement report about Counterpoise itself. A separate workflow reviews these later; nothing happens immediately. Use this for a problem with the app, not for anything about the user's financial data.

description.description: What went wrong or what should improve, in the reporter's own words.

page.description: The app path the report is about, e.g. /b/1/transactions.

type.description: The kind of report: bug, improvement, or other. Defaults to bug.

name: create_payee
title: Create Payee
description: Create a payee in the book. Does not fold case, so 'IKEA' and 'Ikea' are both created as distinct payees, and it does not search for a similar existing payee — use list_payees first to check for one. An EXACT repeat of an existing name in this book fails rather than inserting a second row, since the book allows only one payee per exact name.

name.description: The payee's name. Normalized on save: whitespace runs collapse to one space and curly quotes straighten to '. Case is NOT changed — "IKEA" and "Ikea" stay two different payees.

name: create_recurring_rule
title: Create Recurring Rule
description: Create a recurring transaction rule. templateSplits is the transaction the rule will create each time it fires: at least two splits summing to zero, each on an account in this book. nextDate is computed from startDate and the recurrence fields — you cannot set it here; use update_recurring_rule to move it afterwards. Creating a rule creates no transaction: call process_recurring_rules for that.

name.description: A short label for the rule, shown in the recurring list — "Rent", "Netflix". This is not the description written onto the transactions it creates; that is templateDescription.

frequency.description: How often the rule fires: daily, weekly, monthly or yearly. Combined with interval — monthly with interval 3 is quarterly.

startDate.description: The date the schedule is anchored to, YYYY-MM-DD. nextDate is computed from it and then advanced past today, so a startDate in the past does not make the rule instantly overdue.

endDate.description: The last scheduled date, YYYY-MM-DD, or null for no end. Must not be earlier than startDate. An occurrence scheduled on or before this date still counts even when a business-day shift lands it after.

accountId.description: The account this split posts to. Must be an account in this book.

amount.description: Amount in cents. Positive is a debit, negative a credit. Every split in templateSplits must sum to zero.

templateSplits.description: The transaction this rule creates each time it fires: at least two splits that sum to zero, each on an account in this book.

autoCreateDaysBefore.description: How many days early process_recurring_rules may create an occurrence, 0 to 30. 0 means only on or after the day it is due.

businessDaysOnly.description: When true, an occurrence landing on a weekend is dated the following Monday. The rule's own schedule does not move, so the cadence never creeps. Bank holidays are not modelled.

interval.description: How many frequency units between occurrences, as a positive integer — 1 means every period. Applied to daily, weekly and monthly rules — weekly with interval 4 is every 4 weeks. A weekly rule uses it only while weekOfMonth is unset or 'every'; an nth-week-of-month pattern ignores it, as do yearly rules. Defaults to 1.

daysOfWeek.description: For weekly rules: which weekdays it fires on, as an array of integers, Sunday 0 through Saturday 6. Omit or send null to use the weekday of startDate.

weekOfMonth.description: For weekly rules: which weeks count. "every" (the default), "2" to "5" for every Nth week, or "last" for the final week of the month.

daysOfMonth.description: For monthly rules: which days of the month it fires on, as an array of integers 1 to 31. Omit or send null to use the day of startDate.

templateDescription.description: The description written onto each transaction this rule creates. Null leaves them without one.

payeeId.description: An existing payee id in this book to attach to created transactions. Silently ignored if it does not belong to this book. payeeName wins when both are given.

payeeName.description: A payee name to attach. Matched case-insensitively against this book's payees and CREATED if there is no match. Takes precedence over payeeId.

name: create_security
title: Create Security
description: Create a new security (ETF, mutual fund, or stock) in a book. Fails with an error if a security with the same symbol (case-insensitive) already exists in the book. Set fixedPriceMicros for a security whose price never moves, such as a money market fund at a $1.00 NAV. Doing so forces price fetching off.

bookId.description: The book ID to create the security in

fetchPrices.description: Whether to fetch prices automatically (defaults to true)

fixedPriceMicros.description: Price in micros (1,000,000 = $1.00) that never moves, for a security such as a money market fund held at a fixed NAV. Setting this forces fetchPrices off, since a fixed price and automatic fetching would otherwise contradict each other.

name: create_transaction
title: Create Transaction
description: Create a new transaction with double-entry splits. Each split has an accountId and amount in cents. Positive amounts are debits, negative are credits. The splits must sum to zero, or the transaction is rejected. Optionally include investmentSplits for investment transactions. Use list_accounts to find account IDs first.

payeeName.description: Payee name. Matched case-insensitively to an existing payee in this book; created if none matches.

checkNumber.description: Check number (only for bank account transactions)

isFloating.description: If true, the transaction's effective date auto-advances to today until reconciled. Useful for checks or expected deposits where the clearing date is unknown.

isReconciled.description: If true, the transaction is recorded as already reconciled. If the transaction is floating (isFloating is true), also set isFloating to false and give the cleared date in the same call. If you set only isReconciled, the transaction stays floating, and its effective date keeps moving to today even though it is marked reconciled.

accountId.description: The account ID for this split

amount.description: Amount in cents. Positive = debit, negative = credit. All splits must sum to zero.

investmentSplits.description: Investment splits (required if transaction involves investment accounts)

sharesMicros.description: Number of shares in micros (1,000,000 = 1 share). Always positive.

splitNumerator.description: For stock split: new share ratio numerator

splitDenominator.description: For stock split: old share ratio denominator

name: delete_account
title: Delete Account
description: Delete an account. Refuses to delete an account that still has transactions or sub-accounts — clear or reassign those first. This cannot be undone. Use list_accounts or get_account_tree to find an accountId.

name: delete_book
title: Delete Book
description: Permanently delete a book and ALL of its data — every account, transaction, split, security, price, lot, recurring rule, payee and bank connection in it. This cannot be undone. You must pass confirmBookName exactly matching the book's name; use list_books to read it first. Do not call this unless the user has explicitly asked to delete this specific book.

confirmBookName.description: The book's exact name, as a confirmation that this deletion is intended

name: delete_issue_report
title: Delete Issue Report
description: Permanently delete one of your own issue reports. Use list_issue_reports to find an id.

id.description: The issue report ID to delete.

name: delete_payee
title: Delete Payee
description: Delete a payee. Refuses when the payee still has transactions — reassign or delete those first. This cannot be undone. Use list_payees to find a payeeId.

name: delete_plaid_token
title: Delete Plaid Token
description: Delete a bank connection and its entire reconciliation history. This removes the account mappings, every staged transaction still awaiting review, AND every already-resolved row — the matched, created and ignored ones. Local transactions are not deleted, but those that were matched lose their link to the bank transaction that confirmed them, and the matched history that payee-based auto-matching learns from is gone, so future syncs on a re-added connection will match less well. To discard only the pending queue and re-fetch from scratch, use clear_plaid_sync_data instead. This cannot be undone.

bookId.description: The book ID the connection belongs to

tokenId.description: The Plaid connection ID to delete

name: delete_recurring_rule
title: Delete Recurring Rule
description: Delete a recurring rule and its template splits. Transactions the rule already created are KEPT — their link to the rule is cleared, so they stop appearing in list_recurring_transactions. This cannot be undone; to stop a rule without losing it, set isActive false with update_recurring_rule instead.

ruleId.description: The recurring rule ID to delete

name: delete_security
title: Delete Security
description: Permanently delete a security from a book. Refuses when the security still has investment transactions, so a delete cannot orphan them. This does not protect price history: deleting a security also deletes every price ever recorded for it, even one with no investment transactions at all.

bookId.description: The book ID the security belongs to

name: delete_security_price
title: Delete Security Price
description: Delete one recorded price for a security on a specific date. The security and its other prices are left alone.

bookId.description: The book ID the security belongs to

securityId.description: The security whose price is being deleted

priceDate.description: The date of the price entry to delete (YYYY-MM-DD)

name: delete_transaction
title: Delete Transaction
description: Delete a transaction and all of its splits. This cannot be undone. Any Plaid reconciliation row matched to this transaction returns to pending, and investment lots are rebuilt for every affected security. Use list_transactions or search to find the transaction ID first.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: The updatedAt value you loaded. When you send it and the transaction changed since, the delete is refused (HTTP 409) and nothing changes. Omit it to skip the check.

name: fetch_tiingo_prices
title: Fetch Tiingo Prices
description: Fetch the latest end-of-day price for one or more ticker symbols from Tiingo. Returns prices ([{symbol, price, date}], price in dollars) and errors (symbols that failed). This reads an external service and records nothing. To save a price, find its securityId with list_securities and call set_security_prices with priceMicros = price × 1,000,000. Requires TIINGO_API_KEY to be configured on the server.

bookId.description: The book ID making the request

symbols.description: Ticker symbols to fetch the latest end-of-day price for (e.g. ["VTI", "BND"])

name: get_account_balance_history
title: Get Account Balance History
description: Get the running balance for an account over time, showing each transaction's impact. Useful for tracking balance progression, finding when balances changed, or plotting account trends. Entries run oldest first from startDate, and limit keeps the earliest entries. A range longer than limit therefore loses its most recent entries, and no flag reports this; narrow startDate to see recent activity.

accountId.description: The account ID to get history for

name: get_account_tree
title: Get Account Tree
description: Get a hierarchical tree of all active accounts grouped by type (asset, liability, equity, income, expense). balance and balanceCents are in cents with the ledger sign: liabilities, equity and income are negative. Use list_accounts for display-signed balances, inactive accounts, or a balance as of a date.

name: get_income_statement
title: Get Income Statement
description: Get an income statement (profit & loss) for a date range. Returns all income and expense accounts with their balances, plus totals. Balances are shown as positive numbers (income earned, expenses spent).

name: get_investment_positions
title: Get Investment Positions
description: Get current investment positions across all accounts or for a specific account. Returns each security held with: shares, cost basis, current price, market value, and gain/loss. Optionally get per-account market value totals. Amounts are in dollars and shares in whole units, not cents or micros. Use list_securities for every security in the book with dividend income, and get_security_detail for the history and lots of one security.

includeAccountValues.description: Also include total market value per account

name: get_payee
title: Get Payee
description: Get one payee by ID, with its transaction count and lastAccountId — the account on the largest debit split of its most recent transaction (null when the payee has no transactions). Use list_payees to find a payeeId.

name: get_plaid_status
title: Get Plaid Status
description: The state of a book's bank connections in one call: each connection (with its access token masked, and how many of the bank accounts it exposes are mapped to a Counterpoise account as mappedAccountCount of totalAccountCount), how many synced transactions are waiting to be reconciled, which accounts hold manually-entered transactions no bank transaction has matched, and every Plaid account mapped to a Counterpoise account — its plaidAccountMask (the last digits the bank shows) and its own pending and review counts.

name: get_projected_transactions
title: Get Projected Transactions
description: Project the transactions that active recurring rules WILL create over a date range, without creating anything. Defaults to tomorrow through the book's upcoming-days window. Each projected transaction carries a negative synthetic id and isProjected true — it is not in the ledger and its id cannot be passed to any other tool. Use list_recurring_transactions for occurrences that already happened.

startDate.description: Inclusive start, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to tomorrow.

endDate.description: Inclusive end, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today plus the book's upcomingDays.

accountId.description: Keep only rules with a template split on this account or on a direct child of it. Omit for every rule.

name: get_realized_gains
title: Get Realized Gains
description: Get realized capital gains and losses from investment sales for a date range — the answer to tax-time questions like 'what were my realized capital gains last year'. Returns one row per lot disposed of: a single sell that draws shares from three different purchase lots yields three rows (matching how a 1099-B reports each lot as a separate line), plus totals split into short-term and long-term gain, along with total proceeds and cost basis. A row with term 'unknown' means the sold shares couldn't be matched to a purchase lot — real proceeds but no basis or gain, excluded from the short/long totals and counted in unknownBasisDisposals so a data gap can't silently understate a reported gain. All amounts are in dollars.

accountId.description: Filter to a specific investment account

name: get_reconcile_candidates
title: Get Reconcile Candidates
description: The reconciliation queue for one linked bank account, or for every linked account in the book when plaidAccountLinkId is omitted: every synced transaction still awaiting a decision, plus any already-resolved one the bank has since changed or removed. Each item carries up to five ranked local transactions that might be the same spend, with a score and the reasons behind it, and a suggested counter account drawn from what this payee was categorised as before. Feed an item's id and its plaidAccountLinkId to reconcile_plaid_transaction to resolve it. Rows needing review are listed first; across all accounts, the rest follow newest bank date first.

bookId.description: The book ID the connection belongs to

plaidAccountLinkId.description: The Plaid account link ID, as returned by get_plaid_status in assignedAccounts[].plaidLinkId. Omit to return the queue for all linked accounts.

name: get_report_data
title: Get Report Data
description: Get raw transaction split data for custom analysis. Returns one row per split in the date range, with its account info, effective date, and payee. Rows run oldest first and stop at limit; truncated is true when more rows exist, so the rows dropped are the most recent. Useful for building custom reports, grouping by category/payee/month, etc.

name: get_security_detail
title: Get Security Detail
description: Get detailed information about a specific security including: basic info, current position, price history, and all related transactions.

securityId.description: The security ID to look up

priceLimit.description: Number of recent prices to return (default 50, max 200)

priceOffset.description: Number of most-recent prices to skip before taking priceLimit. Use with priceLimit to page through price history older than the most recent priceLimit rows.

includeLots.description: Include the open FIFO lots for this security — one row per lot with its account, acquisition date, remaining shares, and remaining cost basis. Off by default because most questions do not need lot-level detail.

name: get_system_status
title: Get System Status
description: Report the health of Counterpoise's background jobs: database backup, backup pruning, hourly recurring-transaction processing, bank sync, security price sync, and the monthly database compaction (the job named reindex). Each job reports one of ok, stale, unverified, failed, missing, not_configured (Plaid sync or price sync with no secret set — normal, and the detail names the missing setting), or unknown (no status directory mounted — the normal case in local development). Overall is 'attention' if any job needs it; not_configured and unknown never cause it.

name: get_transaction_plaid_link
title: Get Transaction Plaid Link
description: The staged Plaid row a transaction is matched to. Returns null when the transaction was entered by hand rather than matched to a bank transaction.

bookId.description: The book ID the transaction belongs to

transactionId.description: The transaction ID to look up

name: list_accounts
title: List Accounts
description: List all accounts in a book with their balances. Optionally filter by account type, active status, or compute balances as of a specific date.

asOfDate.description: Compute balances as of this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

name: list_book_members
title: List Book Members
description: List the users who can open a book, with each user's role: owner, editor or viewer. Any member can call this.

name: list_books
title: List Books
description: List the accounting books you can open in Counterpoise, with your role in each (owner, editor or viewer). Returns book IDs, names, roles and creation dates. Use this first to discover which bookId to pass to other tools.

name: list_issue_reports
title: List Issue Reports
description: List the authenticated user's own issue reports, newest first. Never returns another user's reports.

name: list_payees
title: List Payees
description: List payees in the book. Each row carries its transaction count and the date of its most recent transaction (null when unused). Sorted by name. A book imported from another app can hold thousands of payees, so pass search or limit rather than listing them all when you are looking for a particular one.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the payee name. Omit to list every payee.

limit.description: Maximum payees to return, applied after sorting by name. Omit for all.

name: list_pending_plaid_transactions
title: List Pending Plaid Transactions
description: Bank transactions a Plaid sync has staged but nothing has reconciled yet — waiting to be matched to an existing Counterpoise transaction, created as a new one, or ignored. Rows flagged for review (reviewReason) are not included; get_reconcile_candidates returns them.  These are staged bank transactions, not Counterpoise transactions: their ids are synthetic placeholders and must never be passed to create_transaction, update_transaction, delete_transaction, or any other transaction tool.

accountId.description: Limit the results to this Counterpoise account. Omit to return every account.

name: list_plaid_token_accounts
title: List Plaid Token Accounts
description: List the bank accounts a Plaid connection exposes and which Counterpoise account each is mapped to. This reads only local data and never contacts Plaid.

bookId.description: The book ID the connection belongs to

name: list_prices_due
title: List Prices Due
description: List securities in a book that need a manual price entry: those with automatic fetching off, no fixed price, an open position, and no price recorded for the most recent market day. Returns that due date alongside the securities.

name: list_recurring_rules
title: List Recurring Rules
description: List every recurring transaction rule in the book, active and inactive, each with its payee and its template splits. Sorted active first, then by next scheduled date. nextDate is the next SCHEDULED date; with businessDaysOnly set, an occurrence landing on a weekend is dated the following Monday instead. There is no separate get-one tool — read a single rule from this list.

name: list_recurring_transactions
title: List Recurring Transactions
description: List the transactions a recurring rule actually created within a date range, each with the id and name of the rule that created it. Dates are effective dates, so a floating transaction is matched on the date it currently reports. A transaction whose rule was deleted no longer appears here.

startDate.description: Inclusive start of the range, YYYY-MM-DD.

endDate.description: Inclusive end of the range, YYYY-MM-DD.

name: list_securities
title: List Securities
description: List every security in a book with its current position: shares held, cost basis from FIFO lots, latest price, market value, and total dividend and capital-gain income received. Book-wide, so holdings in inactive accounts are included.

name: list_transactions
title: List Transactions
description: Query transactions with optional filters. Returns transactions with their splits (debit/credit entries), payee, and investment details. Use accountId for a single account, or accountIds for several at once. Results are ordered by effective date, newest first. A floating transaction (isFloating) has an effective date of today, so it sorts first and matches date filters as today. effectiveDate is the date used for sorting and filtering; date is the stored entry date.

accountId.description: Filter to transactions involving this account

accountIds.description: Filter to transactions involving ANY of these accounts. Takes precedence over accountId when both are given.

name: process_recurring_rules
title: Process Recurring Rules
description: Create the transactions recurring rules are due for. With processAll true, every active rule is processed up to its own lead window (autoCreateDaysBefore), rules past their endDate are deactivated, and a rule that is not yet due is left alone — so a repeat call creates nothing more. With ruleId, that ONE rule is FORCED: its next occurrence is created and the rule advances whether or not it was due, so calling twice creates two transactions. Passing neither creates nothing. Returns the ids created plus a skipped list naming rules that produced nothing because they have fewer than two template splits.

ruleId.description: Process this ONE rule, forcing its next occurrence whether or not it is due, and advancing the rule. Wins over processAll when both are given.

processAll.description: Process every active rule that is due within its own lead window. Ignored when ruleId is given.

name: reconcile_plaid_transaction
title: Reconcile Plaid Transaction
description: Resolve one staged bank transaction from the reconciliation queue. Six actions: 'match' links it to a transaction you already entered and marks that transaction reconciled; 'match_update_amount' does the same and rewrites the transaction's two splits to the bank's amount (two-split, non-investment transactions only); 'create' writes a new two-split transaction from the bank's data; 'ignore' dismisses the bank transaction; 'keep_local' clears a review flag and keeps what you already have; 'unlink' returns a resolved row to the pending queue and stops its transaction being reconciled, unless another bank row still matches that transaction (a transfer seen on both sides). Matching or creating against a bank row that is already linked is refused — unlink it first. Matching a floating transaction also settles it, clearing its floating flag and stamping the bank's date. Get the reconciliationId and its candidate matches from get_reconcile_candidates first.

bookId.description: The book ID the connection belongs to

plaidAccountLinkId.description: The Plaid account link ID this staged transaction belongs to

reconciliationId.description: The id of the staged Plaid transaction to resolve, from the reconciliation queue.

action.description: What to do with this bank transaction. 'match' links it to an existing transaction; 'match_update_amount' links it and rewrites that transaction's two splits to the bank's amount; 'create' writes a new two-split transaction from it; 'ignore' dismisses it; 'keep_local' clears a review flag and keeps what you already have; 'unlink' returns an already-resolved row to the pending queue.

transactionId.description: The existing transaction to link to. Required for 'match' and 'match_update_amount', ignored otherwise.

counterAccountId.description: The account the other side of the new transaction posts to. Required for 'create', ignored otherwise, and it must not be the account this connection is linked to.

payeeName.description: The payee to record on a created transaction. Only read for 'create'; defaults to the bank's merchant name, then to the raw transaction name. If no payee with this name already exists in the book (case-insensitively), a new payee row is created — an additive, reversible side effect of 'create'.

name: remove_book_member
title: Remove Book Member
description: Remove a user's access to a book. An owner can remove any member. Any member can remove themselves (leave the book). The last owner cannot be removed.

userId.description: The member's user ID, from list_book_members

name: search
title: Search
description: Search across transactions (description, notes, payee, check number, and an exact split amount when the query parses as money: '50' matches ±$50.00), accounts (name), payees (name), and recurring rules (name, template description). Returns up to 25 results per entity type; the accounts, payees, and recurringRules buckets each carry total and truncated so a cut list is never mistaken for a complete one. The transactions bucket has no total, so 25 transactions can be a partial list. Use this for free-text discovery; to filter by account, payee or date without a text query, use list_transactions.

name: set_plaid_token_accounts
title: Set Plaid Account Mapping
description: Map a Plaid connection's bank accounts to Counterpoise accounts. Pass counterpoiseAccountId null to unmap one. This replaces the mapping for every plaidAccountId you list and leaves any you omit alone. Refuses the whole batch if an id is not one of this connection's accounts, is not an account in this book, or is already mapped to a different Plaid account.

bookId.description: The book ID the connection belongs to

plaidAccountId.description: The Plaid account id to assign, from this connection's account list.

counterpoiseAccountId.description: The Counterpoise account id to map this Plaid account to, or null to unmap it. Required on every element — there is no way to leave it out.

assignments.description: The plaidAccountId-to-counterpoiseAccountId mappings to set. Each plaidAccountId you list is replaced with the counterpoiseAccountId given; a plaidAccountId this connection has but you omit is left alone.

name: set_security_prices
title: Set Security Prices
description: Record manual prices for securities in a book. Each entry overwrites any existing price for the same security and date. Entries that are malformed are skipped and reported back in `discarded`; the whole batch is rejected only if no entry is usable, or if any security belongs to a different book.

bookId.description: The book ID the securities belong to

priceUpdates.description: Prices to record. Each entry is an object with securityId (positive integer), priceMicros (positive number, 1,000,000 = $1.00), and priceDate (YYYY-MM-DD).

name: sync_plaid_token
title: Sync Plaid Connection
description: Fetch new, changed and removed transactions from Plaid for one connection and stage them for reconciliation, then run auto-matching. Reaches Plaid and changes data. Returns counts of what was added, modified, removed and auto-matched. A demo connection cannot sync and says so.

bookId.description: The book ID the connection belongs to

tokenId.description: The Plaid connection ID to sync

name: unlink_plaid_transaction
title: Unlink Plaid Transaction
description: Remove a transaction's Plaid link. The bank transaction returns to the pending queue, and the local transaction stops being reconciled — this does not delete anything.

bookId.description: The book ID the transaction belongs to

name: update_account
title: Update Account
description: Update an account's fields. All fields are optional — only provided fields are changed. Use list_accounts or get_account_tree to find an accountId.

subtype.description: New account subtype: bank, credit_card, loan, investment, cash, or other.

parentId.description: New parent account ID, to move this account under it. Send null to make it a top-level account.

isActive.description: Set to false to deactivate the account, or true to reactivate it. For an investment account, this also updates its paired cash sub-account.

isFavorite.description: Set to true to mark the account as a favorite.

icon.description: A single emoji to show for this account. Only income and expense accounts show an icon. Send null to inherit the icon from the parent account instead of setting one directly.

name: update_book
title: Update Book
description: Rename a book, and optionally change how many days ahead it projects recurring transactions. name is always required — to change only upcomingDays, resend the book's current name. Use list_books to read it and to find a bookId.

name.description: The book's name, shown in the book switcher and page titles.

upcomingDays.description: How many days ahead recurring transactions are projected on the dashboard (integer, 1-365). Omit to leave it unchanged.

name: update_book_member
title: Update Book Member
description: Change a member's role. Owner only. A book must keep at least one owner, so the last owner cannot be demoted.

userId.description: The member's user ID, from list_book_members

role.description: owner: everything, including members, rename, delete and bank connections. editor: read and change the ledger. viewer: read only.

name: update_issue_report
title: Update Issue Report
description: Change the description, type, or status of one of your own issue reports. Use list_issue_reports to find an id. At least one field must be given.

id.description: The issue report ID to update.

description.description: New description. Omit to leave it unchanged.

status.description: New status: new, resolved, or wontfix. Omit to leave it unchanged.

type.description: New type: bug, improvement, or other. Omit to leave it unchanged.

name: update_plaid_token
title: Update Plaid Token
description: Replace a bank connection's institution name and item id. This is a full replace, not a patch: financialInstitution and itemId are both required on every call. Rotating the connection's access token is not available through this interface — that credential can only be re-obtained through the Plaid Link browser flow, and this tool does not accept one.

bookId.description: The book ID the connection belongs to

tokenId.description: The Plaid connection ID to update

financialInstitution.description: The bank or brokerage name for this connection. Required.

itemId.description: Plaid's item id for this connection. Required, and must not already belong to another connection in this book.

name: update_recurring_rule
title: Update Recurring Rule
description: Update a recurring rule. Every field is optional and an omitted field is left alone. Passing templateSplits REPLACES every existing template split, so send the complete set. Changing any schedule field (frequency, interval, daysOfWeek, weekOfMonth, daysOfMonth, startDate) recomputes nextDate from startDate unless you pass nextDate yourself, and the recomputed date never moves back before the last transaction this rule already created. To pause a rule, send isActive false rather than deleting it.

ruleId.description: The recurring rule ID to update

startDate.description: The date the schedule is anchored to, YYYY-MM-DD. nextDate is computed from it and then advanced past today, so a startDate in the past does not make the rule instantly overdue.

endDate.description: The last scheduled date, YYYY-MM-DD, or null for no end. Must not be earlier than startDate. An occurrence scheduled on or before this date still counts even when a business-day shift lands it after.

nextDate.description: Force the next scheduled date, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides the recompute that changing a schedule field would otherwise trigger. Omit unless you are deliberately moving the rule.

accountId.description: The account this split posts to. Must be an account in this book.

amount.description: Amount in cents. Positive is a debit, negative a credit. Every split in templateSplits must sum to zero.

templateSplits.description: The transaction this rule creates each time it fires: at least two splits that sum to zero, each on an account in this book.

autoCreateDaysBefore.description: How many days early process_recurring_rules may create an occurrence, 0 to 30. 0 means only on or after the day it is due.

businessDaysOnly.description: When true, an occurrence landing on a weekend is dated the following Monday. The rule's own schedule does not move, so the cadence never creeps. Bank holidays are not modelled.

name.description: A new label for the rule. Omit to leave it unchanged.

frequency.description: How often the rule fires: daily, weekly, monthly or yearly. Combined with interval — monthly with interval 3 is quarterly.

isActive.description: False pauses the rule — it stops projecting and stops being processed, but is kept. Prefer this over delete_recurring_rule for a temporary stop.

interval.description: How many frequency units between occurrences, as a positive integer — 1 means every period. Applied to daily, weekly and monthly rules — weekly with interval 4 is every 4 weeks. A weekly rule uses it only while weekOfMonth is unset or 'every'; an nth-week-of-month pattern ignores it, as do yearly rules. Defaults to 1.

daysOfWeek.description: For weekly rules: which weekdays it fires on, as an array of integers, Sunday 0 through Saturday 6. Omit or send null to use the weekday of startDate.

weekOfMonth.description: For weekly rules: which weeks count. "every" (the default), "2" to "5" for every Nth week, or "last" for the final week of the month.

daysOfMonth.description: For monthly rules: which days of the month it fires on, as an array of integers 1 to 31. Omit or send null to use the day of startDate.

templateDescription.description: The description written onto each transaction this rule creates. Null leaves them without one.

payeeId.description: An existing payee id in this book to attach to created transactions. Silently ignored if it does not belong to this book. payeeName wins when both are given.

payeeName.description: A payee name to attach. Matched case-insensitively against this book's payees and CREATED if there is no match. Takes precedence over payeeId.

name: update_security
title: Update Security
description: Update a security's name, symbol, type, price-fetching setting, or fixed price. Only the fields you pass are changed. Setting fixedPriceMicros forces price fetching off.

bookId.description: The book ID the security belongs to

name.description: New display name for the security

fetchPrices.description: Whether to fetch prices automatically for this security

fixedPriceMicros.description: Price in micros (1,000,000 = $1.00) that never moves, for a security such as a money market fund held at a fixed NAV. Setting this forces fetchPrices off. Pass null to clear it; fetching stays off until you turn it back on.

name: update_security_price
title: Update Security Price
description: Change a recorded price for one security on one date. Pass a different priceDate to move the entry to another date.

bookId.description: The book ID the security belongs to

securityId.description: The security whose price is being changed

currentDate.description: The date of the existing price entry to change (YYYY-MM-DD)

priceDate.description: The date this price applies to (YYYY-MM-DD). Pass a different date to move the entry.

source.description: Where the price came from, such as "manual"

name: update_transaction
title: Update Transaction
description: Update an existing transaction. All fields are optional — only provided fields will be updated. If splits are provided, they replace ALL existing splits (must sum to zero). Use list_transactions or search to find transaction IDs. Pass expectedUpdatedAt from the row you read to refuse the update if someone changed it since.

isFloating.description: Set to true to make the transaction float (effective date = today). Set to false to stop floating.

isReconciled.description: Set to true to mark the transaction reconciled. If the transaction is floating (isFloating is true), also set isFloating to false and set date to the cleared date in the same call. If you set only isReconciled, the transaction stays floating, and its effective date keeps moving to today even though it is marked reconciled.

splits.description: New splits (replaces all existing, must sum to zero)

accountId.description: The account ID for this split

amount.description: Amount in cents. Positive = debit, negative = credit. All splits must sum to zero.

sharesMicros.description: Number of shares in micros (1,000,000 = 1 share). Always positive.

splitNumerator.description: For stock split: new share ratio numerator

splitDenominator.description: For stock split: old share ratio denominator

expectedUpdatedAt.description: The updatedAt value you loaded. When you send it and the transaction changed since, the update is refused (HTTP 409) and nothing changes. Omit it to skip the check.
